q: Polynomial-like maps (Douady-Hubbard) generalize polynomials and are used to explain renormalization. A polynomial-like map of degree d is:
opts: A proper holomorphic map f: U' → U of degree d with U' ⊂⊂ U
A rational map of degree d on ℂ̂
An entire function with d critical points
exp: A polynomial-like map (Douady-Hubbard 1985) is a proper holomorphic map f: U' → U with U', U ⊂ ℂ open and U' ⊂⊂ U. Its filled Julia set K_f = ∩ f⁻ⁿ(U) mimics a polynomial. The straightening theorem shows it is hybrid equivalent to an actual polynomial.
